Title: Volcanic Slopes
Content: During a summer trip, Aiden visits a volcanic island. He learns that the island was formed by `text(six)` volcanoes over `text(millions of years)`. Aiden finds a topographic map that shows the location, elevation, and boundaries of each volcano. A topographic map shows differences in elevation. Each elevation line on the map shows locations that are the same height above sea level. The numbers represent `text(kilometers)` above sea level.
The volcanoes on the map are labeled by numbers `1-6` in the order of age. The oldest volcano, volcano `1`, is underwater. The youngest volcano, volcano `6`, is still forming new parts of the island.

The map shows canyons on `text(two)` of the slopes of volcano `2`. During his trip, Aiden goes for a walk on volcano `2`. As he stands facing the volcano from the `text(south)`, Aiden observes that the western slope of the volcano is steep and rocky with no canyon. The eastern slope of the volcano is not as steep, has a deep canyon, and is covered with plants.
Aiden draws a diagram that shows his observations. He plans an investigation to find out what caused the differences in the `text(two)` slopes of the volcano.
